content.title: About
content.content: Mushrooms are edible fungal fruits that, after cooking, are used as an ingredient in a wide variety of dishes. They have a mild, slightly earthy flavor and a tender, sometimes slightly crisp texture. Cooked mushrooms are commonly added to soups, sauces, stews, pasta, and salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mushrooms belong to a separate kingdom – fungi – and are not plants.
More than 10,000 edible mushroom species exist, but culinary use focuses on button mushrooms, oyster mushrooms, shiitake and porcini.
Heat treatment destroys most toxins present in raw mushrooms, making them safe to eat.
Mushrooms readily absorb aromatic compounds, which is why they are used to boost flavor in many recipes.
In some cultures mushrooms are considered a delicacy and are served in haute cuisine.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Cooked mushrooms provide niacin, riboflavin, thiamine and vitamin B12, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: 100 g of cooked mushrooms contain about 22 kcal, making them an excellent choice for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium in mushrooms has antioxidant properties and supports immune health.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Low fat content and potassium help maintain healthy blood pressure.

items.title: Mushroom allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to certain mushroom varieties.

items.title: Raw mushroom toxicity
items.content: Certain mushroom species contain toxins that are neutralized only by sufficient heating.

items.title: Food poisoning risk
items.content: Improper storage or consumption of spoiled mushrooms can lead to foodborne illness.

items.title: High purine content
items.content: People with gout should limit mushroom intake, as they can raise uric acid levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mushrooms can be sautéed, stewed, baked, or added to soups and sauces. They are often sliced and quickly pan‑fried in olive oil with garlic. Cooked mushrooms pair well with herbs, spices, and cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked mushrooms in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze them in portioned bags after cooling to room temperature.
